BLOCKER: AC5's required single fixture set ("valid + every RESIDENCY_* error incl. schema/invalid-field/toolchain/profile") is incomplete: `residency_conformance.json` has no toolchain/`RESIDENCY_VALIDATOR_UNAVAILABLE` case, no `RESIDENCY_MANIFEST_INVALID`/`UNREADABLE` case, and no over-policy retention case; the mandated parity evidence therefore does not exist.
MAJOR: Three parallel policy implementations (Go `Validate`, Python `packaging.validate_residency`, gate `hard_prefix`) already diverge: Python checks `backup.frequency` case-sensitively while Go lowercases, and Python rejects bool `rotation_days` where Go fails unmarshal — such input yields parity=false and is reported as exit-2 "execution failure", not a policy violation.

Gate `hard_prefix` omits `RESIDENCY_HOME_NOT_ALLOWED` (and `RESIDENCY_REGION_NOT_ALLOWED`), so with `gate_mode=warn` (default until 2027-01-31) a manifest whose `home_region` is not in `allowed_regions` exits 0 — a stated AC invariant is unenforced for ~12 months while `ci-cd-gates.json` declares the gate `blocking: true`.

AC4 requires tests covering `language_rule_review` and precheck (45+ gates); the diff adds no such test/assertion, so the language-rule allow entry for `core/packaging.py` and the new precheck gate are unverified.

Unknown home maps to `RESIDENCY_PROFILE_UNREADABLE`, never `RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME` (regex-passing but profileless home, e.g. "XX"); `test_unknown_home_fails_closed` locks in the wrong code, breaking the frozen AC error-code contract.

Adding ~50 lines of shipped policy logic to `core/packaging.py` via language-rule exception duplicates the Go authority rather than reusing it; parity fixtures are the only anti-drift mechanism and are themselves incomplete (see BLOCKER).
MINOR: Go CLI `--profiles` defaults to `config/residency-profiles` relative to CWD (`go/residencymanifest/...`), silently resolving to a nonexistent path for direct callers; only the Python wrapper passes an explicit path.

`cmd/pfresidency` emits report JSON on profile-load failure regardless of `--report`, and its warn mode downgrades every `Validate` error while the gate's warn hard-blocks a subset — two different warn semantics behind one documented contract.
`residency-gate` registered with `"area": ["packaging"]` may not run when `products/*/residency-manifest.json` or `config/residency-profiles/**` change, i.e. exactly the inputs it validates.

`store-registry` `allow` swallows `test-framework/tests/fixtures/residency_conformance.json` (shipped fixture) instead of registering an owner; the scratch-file entries are unnecessary since tests write to `tmp_path`.
Evidence write failure blocks only on the first error path; `_event(rec)` results are ignored on the "no JSON" and normal paths, so a green run can silently produce no bounded event.
Gate parses the manifest with no size cap (packaging `_load_json` caps at 64KB), and `--project` flows into `residency_path` unvalidated, allowing `products/../..` style traversal on a local tool.
`subprocessors` and `legal_hold` field presence are never validated even though AC1 lists them as part of the populated group shape; `egress: {}` passes both validators.
Warn-mode event records `ok: false` with exit 0, so downstream consumers reading `ok` cannot distinguish "warned" from "failed".
NIT: `build()` emits `residency_warning` as a bare string instead of the stable error-code list used everywhere else.
Test modules re-import `os` inside function bodies instead of at module scope.
Go module `productforge/residencymanifest` is added standalone; no `go.work`/build tooling registration appears in the diff.
SUMMARY: Solid skeleton: explicit `home_region`, profile bounds, frozen codes, bounded event, warn-first lever with expiry — and fail-closed on toolchain/profile errors.

Top risks: the mandated cross-language conformance fixture set is incomplete (BLOCKER), warn mode quietly downgrades the home-in-allowed invariant for a year, and three copies of the policy semantics already disagree on case/type edge cases.
Recommend landing the full AC5 fixture set (incl. toolchain), aligning the gate hard-block list with the frozen-code contract, and de-duplicating policy logic before flipping `gate_mode` to block.
